originalGoal: Assess whether this service is ready for release without changing application source. Audit server/auth.ts for authentication/session expiry vulnerabilities and write reports/auth.md with evidence, reproduction cases, severity and recommended fixes. Separately audit server/storage.ts for crash consistency and data-loss risks and write reports/storage.md with failure scenarios, severity and recommended fixes. Produce reports/release.md using both reports to prioritize blockers, explain tradeoffs and recommend a release decision. Do not implement the fixes in this assessment.

nodes.name: audit_auth_session
nodes.task:
Read-only security audit of the service's authentication/session handling, scoped to server/auth.ts (and the closely related server/users.ts, server/config.ts, and contracts/users.json only as needed to establish how sessions/tokens are issued, validated, and expired). Goal: determine whether authentication and session-expiry behavior is release-ready, and write the findings to reports/auth.md.

Authoritative context (atlas-fixture workspace): server/auth.ts holds the session store as a module-level `sessions` Map of token -> {userId, expiresAt} and exposes `authenticate(token)` returning the mapped userId. Public behavior must not change; this assessment must NOT modify any application source, test, contract, or client file — write only reports/auth.md (create the reports/ directory if needed). Any reproduction harness or snippet you run goes under reports/ as evidence material, never into src/, server/, tests/, clients/, or web/.

reports/auth.md must contain, per finding: the vulnerability/weakness and its concrete consequence (e.g. expiry recorded but never enforced, unbounded session retention, missing revocation/logout, token entropy/guessability, cross-request in-memory state and restart behavior — verify against the actual code rather than assuming this list), the file/line evidence quoted or cited, a reproduction case (a concrete, reproducible sequence or a minimal script under reports/ with the command and observed output), a severity rating with the exploit/impact rationale, and a recommended fix described as guidance only (do not implement it).

Conclude with a short summary table of findings by severity and the single most release-critical item. Keep the report as the deliverable; do not change behavior.

nodes.name: audit_storage_consistency
nodes.task:
Read-only durability audit of the service's persistence layer, scoped to server/storage.ts (with server/config.ts and callers consulted only as needed to see what data is written where and how often). Goal: assess crash consistency and data-loss risk, and write findings to reports/storage.md.

Authoritative context (atlas-fixture workspace): server/storage.ts exposes `save(path, data)` implemented as a single `writeFileSync(path, data)` from node:fs — no temp-file/rename, no fsync of file or parent directory, no locking, no atomic replacement. Confirm this against the code and analyze the real consequences rather than assuming the list above is complete or exact. This assessment must NOT modify any application source, test, contract, or client file — write only reports/storage.md (create reports/ if needed). Any reproduction harness belongs under reports/ as evidence, never in src/, server/, tests/, clients/, or web/.

reports/storage.md must contain, per finding: the failure scenario stated concretely (process crash or power loss mid-write leaving a truncated/partial file; concurrent saves interleaving or last-writer-wins overwrite; write succeeding without durability so data is lost on OS crash; overwrite-in-place corrupting a previously good state), the file/line evidence, an observed or reasoned demonstration — prefer a deterministic, bounded reproduction under reports/ (e.g. a script that exercises save() against a temp path and shows partial-write or no-fsync behavior; avoid slow probabilistic full-filesystem or repeated disk-image experiments), a severity rating with the data-loss blast radius, and a recommended fix described only as guidance (do not implement it).

Conclude with a summary table of findings by severity and the single most release-critical item.

nodes.name: release_readiness_report
nodes.task:
Produce the release go/no-go assessment for the atlas-fixture service at reports/release.md, synthesizing the two already-written audit reports reports/auth.md (authentication/session-expiry findings) and reports/storage.md (crash-consistency/data-loss findings). Do not repeat their audits and do not perform any new code audit — consume their findings, severities, evidence links and recommended fixes.

Hard constraint: this is an assessment only. Do not modify any application source, test, contract, or client file (server/, src/, clients/, web/, tests/, contracts/); the only file you write is reports/release.md.

reports/release.md should cover: a clear release recommendation (ship / ship-with-known-risk / hold) stated up front; the blocker list ranked by release impact, each item traced to its source finding in reports/auth.md or reports/storage.md with severity; the tradeoffs the team accepts either way (e.g. shipping with unenforced session expiry or non-atomic persistence versus delaying for fixes, and what operational mitigations such as restart-on-interval, backups, or short session TTLs buy without a code change); explicit acceptance criteria for what must be fixed before release versus what may be deferred; and a short remediation sequencing recommendation derived from the audits' suggested fixes (guidance only, no implementation). Where the two audits disagree or leave an assumption open, note it rather than inventing a conclusion. If either report is missing or lacks severity/evidence, say so explicitly in release.md instead of filling the gap yourself.

nodes.name: audit_release_compliance
nodes.task:
Independent acceptance check of the read-only release assessment deliverables in the atlas-fixture worktree: reports/auth.md, reports/storage.md, and reports/release.md.

Verify exactly three claims, with focused evidence, and save your verification record to reports/verification.md:
1. Completeness: all three report files exist and each audit finding carries the elements its task required — auth: vulnerability, file/line evidence, reproduction case, severity, recommended fix; storage: failure scenario, evidence, severity, recommended fix; release.md: up-front recommendation, ranked blockers traced to the two audits, tradeoffs, fix-before-release vs defer criteria. Severities must be consistent between the audits and release.md's blocker ranking.
2. Assessment-only constraint: application code was not changed. The expected baseline is server/auth.ts containing only the `sessions` Map of token -> {userId, expiresAt} plus `authenticate(token)` returning the mapped userId, and server/storage.ts containing only `save(path, data)` implemented with `writeFileSync` from node:fs (no temp-file/rename, fsync, or locking added). Confirm no fix was applied anywhere, that no new harness or scratch files leaked into server/, src/, clients/, web/, or tests/, and that every evidence artifact lives under reports/. Run `npm test` (the repo's `node --test` script) and record that the pre-existing tests in tests/ still pass.
3. Evidence integrity: spot-check that each finding's quoted file/line evidence actually matches the current server source, and that reproduction claims are real (a reader can re-run a script under reports/ or follow a stated sequence) rather than asserted.

Repair authority and failure path: you may fix only report artifacts (wording, missing severity labels, broken intra-report cross-references, misfiled evidence under reports/) and rerun the checks above. You must not change application source or add fixes. Report substantive gaps you cannot repair — a finding with no evidence, a fabricated or unreproducible reproduction, a missing severity, an unsupported blocker ranking, or any detected modification to application source — as correction requests for the audit owners. End with `<ACCEPT>` on the final line if all three claims hold, otherwise `<REVISE>` on the final line followed by nothing.

edges.relation: compliance check over all three reports
